newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-NAB offshore units boost result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-NAB offshore units boost result.

text.p: Australia's most profitable bank, National Australia Bank Ltd, on Thursday posted a 6.8 percent rise in net profit to A$2.10 billion for the year to September 30, its fourth consecutive record annual result.
The bank also expected to continue to improve its performance, managing director Don Argus said in a statement accompanying the results.

But the stronger group performance, which exceeded analysts average expectations of a A$2.01 billion net profit, was won mostly from offshore units, which contributed A$650 million or 31 percent of group profits in 1995/96.
By comparison profit after tax from NAB's Australian operations fell to A$1.277 billion for the year to September 30 from A$1.284 billion a year earlier.
But Argus defended the Australian result as creditable amid difficult trading conditions.
"Competition in Australia was stronger than in any other market in which the group operated during the year," he said, adding that NAB's domestic interest margin fell to 3.7 percent from 4.3 percent.
Argus later told reporters Australian margins remained under pressure in the current year but would not elaborate.
Analysts said NAB's Australian margins were hit by the ploughing of Australian capital into last year's US$1.56 billion acquisition of U.S.-based Michigan National Corp.

"Money that was in Australia was used to pay for Michigan National. Therefore, the margins in Australia have fallen, but the main reason they've falling is they've redeployed that capital," one Melbourne-based analyst told Reuters.

Michigan reported an operating profit of A$158 million, before amortisation of goodwill, in the 11 months to September 30. "Michigan National performed in line with our expectations," Argus told reporters at a press conference.

Operating profits from United Kingdom and Irish operations slipped four percent to A$403 million in fiscal 1995/96 mainly due to higher bad and doubtful debt provisioning and an appreciation in the Australian dollar.
However, Argus remained bullish about NAB's stable of banks in the region predicting efficiency gains there over the next 18 months.

"I think you will now start to see hopefully in the next 12 to 18 months the real effect of the economies of scale that you can drive out of those four banks in that environment," Argus said. "It's got a huge upside over there."
"We see a softness in the economy and we feel its prudent at this stage to take some extra provisioning. We've done that around the globe," Argus said.

Despite Argus' confidence in NAB's ability to improve results this year, the bank almost tripled its bad and doubtful debt provisioning to A$333 million in response to slowing economic activity in most of its major markets, a scenario it doesn't expect to change quickly.
"We see a softness in the economy and we feel its prudent at this stage to take some extra provisioning. We've done that around the globe," he said.
NAB would continue to reduce costs in 1995/96, Argus said.
"The opportunity to dip into our costs are boundless," he said.
He declined to give an outlook for branch closures and said staff numbers would fluctuate in line with the bank's growth.
Argus said the bank expected to reap further growth in non banking sources of income, such as funds management.
"They are now becoming a very integral part of the future organisation and they are now starting to contribute quite well and I would expect the trend will continue," Argus said.
-- Justin McCamish 61-3 9286-1435
